Melbourne · Commercial floor plans

Commercial floor plans that make the tenancy easier to lease.

Sixth Vision Commercial draws marketing floor plans for Melbourne warehouses, showrooms, offices and mixed tenancies. The plan sits beside the photographs as the factual layer of the campaign: how the spaces connect, where the access is, and what an occupier needs to see before an inspection.

Request a floor-plan briefCall 0474 126 276

File formats

A marketing drawing, supplied for print and the web.

Plans are supplied as high-resolution images, ready to drop into a listing, a brochure or an information memorandum. If a campaign needs a particular file type, say so in the brief and it can be confirmed before the draw starts.

These are not CAD or architectural working drawings, and they are not a PCA certificate. They are prepared so a leasing or sales enquiry can read the tenancy.

How areas are measured

Measured on site, or taken from figures you supply.

Areas and key dimensions are either measured on site for the marketing plan or taken from figures the client supplies. They are drawn so the showroom, warehouse, offices, amenities and external space read at a glance.

A marketing plan is not a legal survey. Survey, title, planning or certification decisions need the qualified document for that job. Where a figure on the plan comes from the client, that is noted in the brief.

Warehouse & showroom

Operational and customer-facing zones on one tenancy layout.

Office & amenities

Offices, reception, amenities, services and circulation.

Access

Roller doors, courtyard or hardstand, where they were part of the brief.

Turnaround

Photography can move in a day. The plan follows the deadline.

24-hour delivery is available for commercial photography. A floor plan is scoped around the campaign deadline, with the address, access and whether the areas are to be measured on site or taken from figures you already hold.

Plans can be booked with commercial property photography, drone photography and measured site plans.

Questions

Before the floor-plan brief.

Which properties can be drawn?

Warehouses, showrooms, offices, mixed office-and-warehouse tenancies and development floors, depending on access.

Can the plan be booked with photography?

Yes. Stills, drone, film, floor plans and site mapping can be one brief. See the portfolio for the kind of work that sits beside a plan.

Is this a survey or a PCA plan?

No. It is a marketing drawing. It does not replace a survey, an architectural set or a PCA certificate.
